security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel loads any RISC-V ELF binary with EF_RISCV_RVY (0x40) set in e_flags, unaware that it targets a CHERI pure-capability ABI, because elf_check_arch at arch/riscv/include/asm/elf.h:37 inspects only e_machine and EI_CLASS — e_flags is completely ignored and no arch_check_elf exists for RISC-V
security_spec.summary: RISC-V kernel has zero e_flags validation: a CHERI pure-capability binary (EF_RISCV_RVY) would silently load on a non-CHERI kernel, executing capability-aware code as bare-pointer code leading to undefined pointer corruption

findings.finding: elf_check_arch inspects only e_machine==EM_RISCV and EI_CLASS but completely ignores e_flags. An ELF binary with EF_RISCV_RVY (0x40) set — targeting the CHERI pure-capability ABI where all memory accesses use hardware capabilities instead of integer addresses — passes this gate unconditionally. No EF_RISCV_* constants are defined anywhere in the kernel tree (git grep returns zero results), so the kernel has no vocabulary to recognize or reject CHERI-ABI binaries.

spec_citations.excerpt: implementations which do not support {cheri_default_ext_name} are typically referred to as CHERI purecap.

Software is referred to as purecap if it utilizes CHERI capabilities for all memory accesses -- including loads, stores and instruction fetches -- rather than integer addresses. Purecap software requires the CHERI RISC-V hart to support {cheri_base_ext_name}.

findings.finding: compat_elf_check_arch (used for 32-bit compat ELF loading via fs/compat_binfmt_elf.c) also does NOT inspect e_flags. Only checks compat_mode_supported, e_machine==EM_RISCV, and EI_CLASS==ELFCLASS32. A 32-bit CHERI purecap binary with EF_RISCV_RVY set would also pass.

arch_check_elf() is called here as a second-layer validation gate after the primary elf_check_arch() passes. RISC-V does NOT override arch_check_elf (no arch/riscv/kernel/elf.c exists, no CONFIG_ARCH_BINFMT_ELF_STATE selected in arch/riscv/Kconfig), so the dummy fallback at fs/binfmt_elf.c:616-621 is used, which unconditionally returns 0 (proceed). Contrast: MIPS (arch/mips/kernel/elf.c:135) and ARM64 (arch/arm64/include/asm/elf.h:289) both override arch_check_elf to inspect e_flags before allowing the exec to proceed. This is the missing hook that should have caught EF_RISCV_RVY.

Default/dummy arch_check_elf() — always returns 0 (proceed). Only compiled when the architecture does NOT provide its own override (i.e., CONFIG_ARCH_BINFMT_ELF_STATE is not selected). RISC-V relies on this dummy, meaning no architecture-specific ELF validation occurs after elf_check_arch passes.

RISC-V Kconfig does NOT select ARCH_BINFMT_ELF_STATE. This means the struct arch_elf_state is empty (generic dummy), arch_elf_pt_proc() is a dummy that ignores PT_LOPROC..PT_HIPROC phdrs, and arch_check_elf() is the generic always-return-0 stub. Contrast: ARM64 (arch/arm64/Kconfig:16), MIPS (arch/mips/Kconfig:6), and LoongArch (arch/loongarch/Kconfig:11) all select ARCH_BINFMT_ELF_STATE to enable arch-specific ELF validation — specifically to inspect e_flags.

findings.finding: First ELF arch-validity check in load_elf_binary(). elf_check_arch(elf_ex) expands to the RISC-V macro that ignores e_flags. An RVY CHERI purecap binary passes this gate and execution continues without any further e_flags inspection at this point.

Same elf_check_arch() gate applied to the ELF interpreter (ld.so). An RVY purecap dynamic linker would also pass unchecked, meaning the CHERI-ABI dynamic linker would be loaded into a non-CHERI kernel address space.
